description: Looking for teammates skilled in Space & Earth Sciences, Data Management, and Storytelling for the NASA Space Apps Challenge!
summary:
SPHEREx Cosmic Detective is an interactive astronomical data exploration and visualization platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. Our project aims to make complex SPHEREx mission data easier to access, understand, process, and visualize.

We developed a platform that integrates React.js and TypeScript for the frontend, Node.js and Express.js for backend communication, and Python with Astropy for scientific data processing. It supports FITS image handling, astronomical coordinate transformations using World Coordinate System (WCS), and interactive sky visualization through Aladin Lite.

The platform addresses the challenge by connecting astronomical datasets with scientific processing and interactive visualization, helping users explore celestial regions, image data, spectral information, and astronomical coordinates.

This project is important because it simplifies the exploration of complex infrared astronomical data and makes scientific information more accessible for students, researchers, and astronomy enthusiasts. Our goal is to bridge the gap between complex space data and understandable cosmic discoveries.
details:
SPHEREx Cosmic Detective is an interactive astronomical data exploration platform designed to help users investigate changes in celestial objects over different observation periods using NASA's SPHEREx mission data.

The project allows users to search for astronomical objects using Right Ascension (RA) and Declination (Dec) coordinates and explore their observations across different epochs. It aims to make complex astronomical data easier to understand through time-lapse visualization, image stacking, image subtraction, spectral analysis, and astronomical catalog integration.

The system processes astronomical observations to help identify changes in brightness, movement, and other observable variations. Image stacking combines compatible observations to improve signal quality, while image subtraction compares different observation periods to highlight changes. Spectral analysis helps users examine the relationship between wavelength and flux. The platform also aims to integrate Gaia DR3 and WISE catalog information to provide additional scientific context.

The project offers several benefits. It makes astronomical data more accessible, reduces the complexity of comparing multiple observations, supports scientific exploration, and helps students, researchers, and astronomy enthusiasts investigate celestial objects. Its intended impact is to encourage data-driven astronomical discovery and make large-scale space mission datasets easier to explore and interpret.

Technologies and tools: The project is being developed using Python, FastAPI, NumPy, SciPy, Astropy, and astronomical FITS data-processing tools for backend and scientific computations. React and JavaScript are used for the web application interface. Firebase services are planned for authentication and data management, while GitHub and cloud development tools support development and collaboration. No additional physical hardware is required because the project primarily works with digital astronomical datasets.

The creative aspect of SPHEREx Cosmic Detective is its combination of multiple scientific analysis techniques in one platform. Instead of simply displaying astronomical images, it aims to let users investigate how celestial objects change across observation periods and examine the scientific evidence behind those changes.

During development, our team considered scientific accuracy, actual NASA data availability, coordinate precision, observation timing, image alignment, noise, data quality, usability, and computational limitations. Our main priority is to ensure that scientific results are based on real observations rather than simulated discoveries.

Our vision is to turn astronomical data exploration into an interactive scientific investigation experience, helping users become cosmic detectives.
dataRefs: This resource provides access to publicly available NEOSSat astronomical data through the Canadian Space Agency's open data directory. It serves as a source for accessing astronomical observation files that can support research and analysis of celestial objects. These observations can be useful for studying changes in brightness, tracking objects, and exploring astronomical phenomena over time.

The NEOSSat Astronomy Dataset is provided by the Canadian Space Agency and includes astronomical images collected by the Near-Earth Object Surveillance Satellite (NEOSSat). Launched on February 25, 2013, NEOSSat is designed to observe and track asteroids, satellites, and other space objects. This dataset provides valuable observational resources for astronomical research, image analysis, and studying the behaviour of celestial objects.

The Canadian Astronomy Data Centre (CADC), operated by the National Research Council of Canada, provides access to astronomical data collections and research services. It archives NEOSSat observations and provides different data products, including raw images, cleaned images, corrected images, and dark-frame-subtracted images. These resources can support astronomical image processing, photometric analysis, object tracking, and scientific investigation.

Gaia is an all-sky astronomical survey mission that measures the positions, distances, proper motions, and physical characteristics of more than a billion stars. The Gaia data available through the Mikulski Archive for Space Telescopes (MAST) can support astronomical research, coordinate-based object identification, stellar analysis, and cross-matching with other astronomical datasets. Its astrometric and photometric information can provide additional scientific context when investigating celestial objects.
